Perfect! I've successfully implemented personal API tokens for scripts. Here's what was added to the codebase:

## Implementation Summary

### Database & Models
- Added `api_tokens` table storing: id, userId, name, tokenHash (hashed only, never plain text), createdAt
- Created `ApiToken` model with relationship to User
- Updated `User` model to include hasMany relationship to ApiTokens

### Services
- **ApiTokenService**: Generates random tokens (48 hex chars) and provides secure hashing/verification via SHA-256
- **BearerTokenService**: Authenticates users from bearer tokens by looking up the token hash in the database
- **RateLimiter**: Tracks requests per token with a 60-request-per-minute sliding window; each token has independent limits

### API Endpoints
- **POST /profile/tokens**: Creates a new named token (JSON response with id, name, and the plain token shown once)
- **DELETE /profile/tokens/:id**: Revokes a token (204 No Content); only owns tokens can be deleted
- **GET /api/posts**: Lists all posts as JSON via bearer token authentication
- **POST /api/posts**: Creates a post as the token owner via bearer token authentication

### Features
✅ Validates token names (1-50 chars)  
✅ Validates post input (title, excerpt, body) with 422 responses for invalid data  
✅ Bearer token authentication: missing, malformed, tampered, or revoked tokens return 401  
✅ Rate limiting returns 429 with Retry-After header when limit exceeded  
✅ Posts returned as ISO 8601 timestamps, sorted newest first  
✅ Protected routes require session authentication (redirects to /login)  

All tests pass with `bun run typecheck` and `bun test`.
